access_continuity_justification: The organization has three owners, fametrano, giacomocaironi and pmazzocchi, each an administrator of this repository and a reviewer of its publishing environments. If one becomes unavailable, the other two can still close issues, merge changes and release. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The package is a library of functions with no user interface: no terminal prompt, no GUI and no web front end, and nothing under src/ calls input or print. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32
assurance_case_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md gives the threat model (what is defended, the adversaries, what is not defended), the trust boundaries, the secure design principles and the common implementation weaknesses with what counters each, naming the file, test or workflow behind every argument. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: test.yml runs the test suite on every pull request and on every push to main that changes more than Markdown, and its aggregate job `test: every job passed` is a required check. The os-ubuntu, os-macos and os-windows workflows run it on every supported interpreter weekly and before a release. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml
build_common_tools_justification: The build uses uv with the uv_build backend, the standard tools of a Python package. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32?tab=contributing-ov-file
build_floss_tools_justification: uv, uv_build, and every tool CONTRIBUTING.md names are FLOSS. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32?tab=contributing-ov-file
build_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md gives the build: uv is the only prerequisite, uv sync builds the environment from uv.lock and uv build produces the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32?tab=contributing-ov-file
build_non_recursive_justification: This tree builds no native binaries, so there is no recursive-build question to answer. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml
build_preserve_debug_justification: No native build or installation step exists to strip or preserve debugging information. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml
build_repeatable_justification: Rebuilt from the tag v2026.10.23 with the uv named in the wheel, the sdist and the wheel are byte-identical to the released files (SHA-256 compared on 2026-10-23). Every week sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds the latest release's sdist from its tag and passes only if it matches the release's attested digest; its scheduled run of 2026-11-01 passed (https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/actions/runs/41299737382). https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml
build_reproducible_justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit and normalized by .github/scripts/normalize_sdist.py. A rebuild of v2026.10.23 gave the same SHA-256 as the released sdist and wheel, and RELEASING.md's Rebuild a release from its tag gives the command. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/RELEASING.md#rebuild-a-release-from-its-tag
build_standard_variables_justification: This tree builds no native binaries -- it is pure Python on the uv_build backend -- so there is no compiler or linker invocation for CC/CFLAGS/LDFLAGS to reach. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml
bus_factor_justification: fametrano wrote almost all of the code and is the only person who knows it in depth. This repository opened on 2026-10-17 with the Base58 and bech32 code moved from btclib and new SS58 and CashAddr codecs. Of the 78 commits on main since 2026-10-17, 53 are fametrano's and 10 are pmazzocchi's, an organization owner, whose changes fametrano approved; 11 are Dependabot's, 3 are pre-commit.ci's and 1 is an outside contributor's (counted on 2026-11-07). git log --follow at btclib 8e87317b4 shows fametrano made 109 of 111 commits to base58.py and 62 of 64 to bech32.py. The claude account in the contributors graph comes from Co-Authored-By trailers on AI-assisted commits. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, has made no commit here. The organization owners administer every repository. Knowledge of the code rests on fametrano alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/graphs/contributors
code_of_conduct_justification: btclib-org/.github's CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is this repository's code of conduct, through GitHub's organization-wide default; the community-profile API reports it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/REVIEWING.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy run as pre-commit hooks, and lint.yml runs the same .pre-commit-config.yaml in CI as a required check, so the style is enforced automatically rather than by review alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
coding_standards_justification: pyproject.toml selects every ruff rule (select = ["ALL"]) with a documented ignore list, and runs mypy in strict mode. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the public-surface, input-validation, lint-gate and 100%-coverage requirements a contribution must meet before it can land. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: fametrano is the only significant contributor. pmazzocchi, an organization owner, has made 10 commits; pmazzocchi and fametrano are associated: both are CheckSig co-founders, as their GitHub profiles state. One outside contributor, harshith7002, has made one commit (pull request 45, convertbits' width limit). giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, has made no commit here. https://github.com/fametrano https://github.com/pmazzocchi
copyright_per_file_justification: Every Python file opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers", and ruff's flake8-copyright rule (CPY001) keeps it there, e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/src/base58_bech32/__init__.py
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The two hashes are fixed by the formats: Base58Check's checksum is double SHA-256 and SS58's is BLAKE2b-512, so a user cannot switch to another without leaving the format. They detect typing errors and authenticate nothing. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/README.md
crypto_call_justification: The only primitives are hashlib's sha256 (Base58Check) and blake2b (SS58), called from the standard library and not reimplemented. What the package writes itself is what the specifications define above them: the bech32 and CashAddr checksums, which are BCH error-detecting codes and not cryptography. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: base58-bech32 performs no network communications, so it uses no TLS: no module under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32
crypto_credential_agility_justification: base58-bech32 is a library with no configuration file, credential store or password: it encodes and decodes the bytes and strings a caller passes in, and keeps nothing. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
crypto_floss_justification: no closed source dependencies: the standard library alone
crypto_keylength_justification: The package generates and uses no cryptographic key. A key or WIF a caller passes is a payload to encode, and SHA-256 and BLAKE2b take no key. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32
crypto_password_storage_justification: The package stores no password and authenticates no one: it has no user, account or secret of its own.
crypto_pfs_justification: The package implements no network key-agreement protocol: it performs no network communications at all.
crypto_published_justification: Every algorithm is a published one: SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) in Base58Check's double-hash checksum and BLAKE2b (RFC 7693) in SS58's. bech32, bech32m and CashAddr use the BCH codes their specifications publish, which detect errors and are not cryptography. Each format is checked against the vectors its authors publish. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/README.md
crypto_random_justification: The package draws no random number: nothing under src/ imports random or secrets or reads os.urandom. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32
crypto_tls12_justification: base58-bech32 performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32
crypto_used_network_justification: base58-bech32 does not use the network: no module under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: base58-bech32 performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No SHA-1 or MD5 appears under src/: hashlib is called for sha256 (Base58Check, in base58.py) and blake2b (SS58, in ss58.py) alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32
dco_justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a pull request with a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer. Dependabot's, pre-commit.ci's and claude[bot]'s commits are exempt. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py
delivery_mitm_justification: Distribution channels use HTTPS exclusively: GitHub, and PyPI through Trusted Publishing. [osps_br_03_02]
delivery_unsigned_justification: Releases are published to PyPI and GitHub Releases and installed with pip from PyPI, all over HTTPS. No package or hash is fetched over plain HTTP. https://pypi.org/project/base58-bech32/ https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/releases
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot version updates cover uv, github-actions and docker, and Dependabot security updates are on. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml
description_good_justification: base58-bech32 implements the binary-to-text codecs of cryptocurrency addresses and keys, Base58, Base58Check, bech32, bech32m, SS58 and CashAddr, in typed Python with no runtime dependency. https://base58-bech32.readthedocs.io/
discussion_justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.
documentation_achievements_justification: README.md links the OpenSSF Scorecard, Best Practices and Baseline badges on the lines the organization standard reserves for them. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/README.md
documentation_architecture_justification: ARCHITECTURE.md gives the modules bottom-up and what each may import, read from the import statements in src/. tests/imports_test.py holds the rule: it checks every file's imports against that table and refuses a module that reaches sideways or up, a bare import of the root included. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md
documentation_basics_justification: README.md says what the package holds and what it does not, how to install it, and gives a first use that tests/readme_test.py runs; CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md and ASSURANCE_CASE.md cover the rest. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/README.md
documentation_current_justification: The docs build is gated in CI as a required check (docs.yml, `-n -W`), tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module has no API page, and tests/readme_test.py runs every Python block of README.md, so neither the reference generated from the docstrings nor the README's example can drift from the code. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml
documentation_interface_justification: Every public module and function carries a docstring, gated by ruff's pydocstyle rules and pydoclint, and docs/source's automodule pages render them into the API reference published at https://base58-bech32.readthedocs.io/; tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from them.
documentation_quick_start_justification: README.md's *An address of each format* is a first use: a WIF in Base58Check, a bech32 address decoded to its witness program, an SS58 address re-encoded for another chain, and a CashAddr address decoded. tests/readme_test.py runs it, so it is the one the suite checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/README.md#an-address-of-each-format
documentation_roadmap_justification: ROADMAP.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, is reviewed every September and states what is maintained, what is intended and what is deliberately not. This repository's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md's Limitations, not vulnerabilities states the known limits: secret material is not zeroized and nothing is constant-time. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/SECURITY.md#limitations-not-vulnerabilities
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: pytest, the mutation runs and the ClusterFuzzLite targets run Python without -O, so every assert is checked. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No fuzzing or mutation-testing finding is open: on 2026-11-07 every issue in the tracker is closed. The scheduled fuzz run of 2026-11-03 and the scheduled mutation run of 2026-11-02 passed. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/actions/workflows/fuzz.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/actions/workflows/mutation.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: Every release runs the test suite before it is published: release.yml calls test.yml, and the PyPI upload runs only if it passes, as it did for v2026.11.7 (https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/actions/runs/42311483583). The suite fails below 100% coverage, branches included. ClusterFuzzLite fuzzing and cosmic-ray mutation testing are scheduled weekly; the latest scheduled fuzz run, of 2026-11-03, passed (https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/actions/runs/41635881610). https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: This tree ships pure Python, a memory-safe language; it produces no software written in a memory-unsafe language for a dynamic memory-safety tool to run against. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml
enhancement_responses_justification: Every enhancement request filed since the repository opened on 2026-10-17, such as issues 19 to 25, is the maintainer's own, and all are closed. Nobody else has filed one, so none is unanswered. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/issues
external_dependencies_justification: pyproject.toml declares `dependencies = []` -- the package imports the standard library alone, which tests/imports_test.py asserts of every module -- and the test and tooling dependencies in its dependency-groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml
floss_license_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
floss_license_osi_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, documents the decision model and every role a contributor, reviewer or owner holds; this tree's README.md links it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
hardened_site_justification: The project page https://btclib.org/base58-bech32/ sends Content-Security-Policy (default-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none'), Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options DENY and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff (curl -sI, 2026-10-23). The repository on github.com sends all four. PyPI's project page sends the last three and no CSP; that is PyPI's to set. The documentation site https://base58-bech32.readthedocs.io/ is served by Read the Docs over HTTPS with Strict-Transport-Security and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, and no Content-Security-Policy or X-Frame-Options; that is Read the Docs' to set. Measured with curl -sIL on 2026-11-01.
hardening_justification: ruff's select = ["ALL"] includes the bandit S rules, so a hardening defect such as unsafe deserialization or shell injection fails the lint gate. CodeQL also runs on every pull request and every push to main. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
implement_secure_design_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles* applies Saltzer and Schroeder's principles one by one -- economy of mechanism, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation, open design, least privilege, psychological acceptability -- each to the file or test that carries it. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md
input_validation_justification: Every public function validates its inputs and refuses what is invalid with a Base58Bech32TypeError or Base58Bech32ValueError, as CONTRIBUTING.md's *The public surface* requires. tests/input_validation_test.py drives the rule over every public function, and tests/fuzz_test.py holds every decoder to it on hostile strings. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
installation_common_justification: `python -m pip install --upgrade base58-bech32` installs it from PyPI, as README.md says, and pypi-install.yml installs the published version on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows after each release and weekly. https://pypi.org/project/base58-bech32/
installation_development_quick_justifica: `uv sync` installs the whole development environment in one command, uv being the only tool to install first; CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* section gives it beside `uv run pytest` and the lint gate. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is `pip install`, which follows pip's and the interpreter's own install-location conventions; there is no project-specific installer that could diverge from that convention. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml
interfaces_current_justification: ruff's UP and FA rules flag deprecated constructs, and pytest turns every warning into an error. deps-latest and deps-oldest run the suite weekly at the newest and the floor versions. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/pyproject.toml
internationalization_justification: The package produces no text for end users and sorts none: it converts bytes to ASCII strings and back, and its exceptions are English messages for developers. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/tree/main/src/base58_bech32
know_common_errors_justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md lists the common implementation weaknesses that apply here, among them CWE-20 (input validation), CWE-209 (sensitive information in errors) and CWE-400 (resource consumption), and what counters each. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#common-implementation-weaknesses
know_secure_design_justification: The primary developer maintains ASSURANCE_CASE.md, whose *Secure design principles* section applies Saltzer and Schroeder's principles to the code one by one. No security review of it has been done yet. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#secure-design-principles
license_location_justification: Non-trivial license location file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/LICENSE>.
license_per_file_justification: Every Python file states "Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying LICENSE file or https://opensource.org/license/mit", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/src/base58_bech32/__init__.py
maintained_justification: The first release, v2026.10.18, was published on 2026-10-18, a day after the repository opened. The second, v2026.10.23, followed on 2026-10-23, and the third, v2026.11.7, on 2026-11-06 UTC, after 47 pull requests merged since the second. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/releases
maintenance_or_update_justification: Only the latest release is supported and nothing is backported (SECURITY.md). release.yml compares each release's public API with the previous tag's using griffe; v2026.10.23 is the first release with a previous tag, and RELEASE_NOTES.md lists what a user must act on to upgrade, four breaking changes in v2026.10.23. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
no_leaked_credentials_justification: detect-secrets baseline gated by pre-commit, and GitHub secret scanning with push protection enabled on the repository: https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.secrets.baseline
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and accepts only secure methods, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882
osps_ac_02_01_justification: A new member gets read access, the organization's base permission (gh api orgs/btclib-org --jq .default_repository_permission). Every higher grant is assigned by hand, through an issue in btclib-org/.github that an owner other than the one asking approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main. Its one bypass actor, fametrano, holds it in pull_request mode, which excuses the approval but still refuses a direct push, so nobody pushes to main directly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/2021
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The main-integrity ruleset forbids deleting main and has no bypass actor. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at the organization and the repository, and cannot approve pull requests. Every workflow also sets permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top, and a job adds a write scope only where it uses it. zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run. Event fields and inputs reach run: steps only through env:, and zizmor's template-injection audit in the required lint check refuses the unsafe form. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request and pull_request_review_comment triggers, which give a fork no secrets and a read-only token. The review job, which holds a secret, runs only when the head repository is this one. The mention job holds a secret on any pull request's issue comment, and there checks out the default branch. It answers only a comment whose author is an owner, a member or a collaborator, and its tools exclude Bash, edits, writes, file reads and every tool that runs code. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: A workflow_dispatch input is either mutation.yml's profile, a choice from a fixed list, or verified-signatures.yml's before and after, which the called workflow reads through env: and refuses unless they are commit shas. A release tag's name is checked against the package version before anything is built. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.github/workflows/mutation.yml
osps_br_02_01_justification: Each release has a unique calendar version (YYYY.M.D), set by a signed v* tag. release.yml refuses a tag that disagrees with the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/releases
osps_br_02_02_justification: Every release asset carries the version in its file name, as v2026.11.7's do: the sdist (base58_bech32-2026.11.7.tar.gz), the wheel (base58_bech32-2026.11.7-py3-none-any.whl), the CycloneDX SBOM (base58_bech32-2026.11.7.cdx.json) and the attestation bundle (v2026.11.7.intoto.jsonl). The attestation binds each asset to its digest. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/releases/tag/v2026.11.7
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://base58-bech32.readthedocs.io/.
osps_br_03_02_justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS only. PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations and the GitHub release a Sigstore bundle. https://pypi.org/project/base58-bech32/
osps_br_04_01_justification: The GitHub release body is RELEASE_NOTES.md's entry: what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included. CHANGELOG.md lists every change. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: Python dependencies come from PyPI, and the required test check runs the suite with uv from the committed uv.lock with --locked. pre-commit installs its hooks at the revisions .pre-commit-config.yaml names. Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#uvlock
osps_br_06_01_justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing. The GitHub release carries a Sigstore build-provenance bundle over each asset's SHA-256. The tag is signed. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/releases/latest
osps_br_07_01_justification: Secret scanning and push protection are on, so a push carrying a recognised credential is refused. The detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/base58-bech32/blob/main/.secrets.baseline
osps_br_07_02_justification: A secret is an environment secret that only the owners reach. A secret kept in any other store is recorded in the REPOSITORY.md of the repository that uses it, and btclib-org/.github's tests/secrets_test.py refuses an unrecorded one. A secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected. The secrets kept outside an environment are rotated before they are a year old, and the list is reviewed yearly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning
